name: passt
desc: User-mode networking daemons for virtual machines and namespaces
why: A user-mode networking daemon that opens a door into how VMs and namespaces actually reach the network.

brief.what_it_is: passt is described by its Homebrew formula as user-mode networking daemons for virtual machines and namespaces. I could not read the project's own pages, so this comes only from that one-line description and the scout note, which calls it a user-mode networking daemon that shows how VMs and namespaces reach the network. The formula installs six executables: passt, passt-repair, passt.avx2, pasta, pasta.avx2 and pesto. I have not confirmed what each one does or what it takes in and produces.
brief.why_it_exists: Not verified. The formula description suggests it provides networking for VMs and namespaces without needing root-level network plumbing, but I could not read the author's framing.
brief.install_notes: Installed via Homebrew under the formula name passt. I found no information on hardware, accounts, runtimes, configuration or first-run steps because no project page loaded.
brief.standout: The formula ships both plain and AVX2-optimised builds (passt and passt.avx2, pasta and pasta.avx2), which hints at a performance-sensitive packet path. The name pasta and the tool pesto suggest a family of related utilities. I have not confirmed any of this against the project's documentation.
brief.status: unknown. Every fetch returned HTTP 404, so I found no last release date, commit date or maintenance note.
brief.caveats: The homepage was unreachable: https://passt.top/passt/about/, https://passt.top/, https://passt.top/passt/ and https://github.com/containers/passt all returned HTTP 404. Everything beyond the formula description and executable names is unverified, and the brief has no commands, quotes or documentation links. The GitHub URL was my own guess at the upstream repository, not something the formula supplied, and it also failed. A writer should re-check the project before publishing.
